pos.personaBrief: 1970 Brazil was built to defend with the ball and counter fast via Gerson, not to hog possession; vs Italy he used possession to tire man-markers.

pro.personaBrief: Quick transitions after winning the ball (Gerson) and a safe single pivot, with 1998 building from Taffarel and a double pivot; shoot-on-sight in 1974.

est.personaBrief: Five 10s interchanged constantly and Rivellino was no fixed winger, but Zagallo demanded discipline and defined duties (Tostao, Pele dropping to help midfield).

lar.personaBrief: Extra central playmakers in the Five 10s, best players central, with width supplied by overlapping full-backs (Carlos Alberto, 1998 full-backs) rather than fixed wingers.

blo.personaBrief: Mixed: back line pushed to halfway when attacking, but a low 4-4-1-1 block against structured attacks; heat made high pressing unrealistic and defensive cohesion came from Feola.

mar.personaBrief: Mostly zonal coverage (1974 blamed on zonal marking) but he told Jair to mark the opposing full-back and expected man-marking from Italy; pragmatic hybrid leaning zone.

pla.personaBrief: He changed system and players to fit the World Cup and adapted tactics to opponents (anticipating Italy's man-marking, instructing Jair), imposing his ideas on arrival.

res.personaBrief: Winner mentality: 'you do not win a World Cup with club basics', discipline and defensive cohesion, results over beauty, though Brazil 1970 was spectacular.

sis.personaBrief: Demanded self-sacrifice from all, including Pele and Tostao, yet wanted his best players always on the pitch, even in unfamiliar roles.

jog.personaBrief: 1970 team full of technicians (Gerson, Rivellino, Pele) but with demanding physical preparation in Guanajuato; 1998 double pivot of Dunga and Sampaio.

bas.personaBrief: National team coach choosing the best available, often established names and recalls (Piazza moved, Tostao), trusting seasoned players; Romario/Ronaldo decisions favored stars.

lid.personaBrief: First meeting demanded discipline and order; he curbed Jair's freedom and called himself the boss, though he bent for Ronaldo in 1998.
